newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to sell Svyazinvest, Transneft stakes.
newsitem.headline: Russia to sell Svyazinvest, Transneft stakes.

text.p: Russia intends to sell 24 percent of telecommunications holding company AO Svyazinvest and 24 percent of monopoly oil pipeline operator AO Transneft next year, according to a copy of the 1997 draft budget obtained by Reuters.
The draft said the Svyazinvest stake would be sold in a commercial tender to raise 1.8 trillion roubles. The Transneft stake would be sold at auction for 640 billion roubles.
The draft said Russia was budgeting for 5.025 trillion roubles in revenue from privatisation and management of state property in 1997.
Of this sum, 4.15 trillion would come from privatisation and 846 billion roubles from managing state property, including dividend income and leasing property.
The document, which was discussed by the cabinet last week, said that in order to achieve the planned revenues a new method of evaluating the charter capital of privatised companies would be used.
It said this would bring the charter capital as close as possible to the true value of the companies' assets.
Workers, who have been able to take shares in their companies, would no longer have privileges and the state would use market methods in setting prices of shares and property to be sold.
Russia tried to sell 25 percent of Svyazinvest in an investment tender late last year.
Italy's Stet SpA won the auction and investment tender but the deal fell through before completion.
Stet agreed to pay $1.3 billion in cash and investment but refused to pay a deposit before Svyazinvest's local telecom companies were registered. The government refused to do this.
The government, which said from the beginning that it ultimately planned to sell 49 percent of Svyazinvest, has said it intends to re-offer the 25 percent stake in a new tender later this year.
Privatisation officials have said the government will focus on a small number of big privatisation deals this year.
Officials said in May the state would sell off 34 percent stakes in five oil companies -- Sibneft, Sidanko, Vostochnaya, Onako and Norsi-oil.

The Federal Property Fund is seeking investment of at least $77 million in Sibneft. It is offering an initial 19 percent later this month at a starting price of 82.38 billion roubles but the winner must also agree to invest the equivalent of $43.48 million.
A 34 percent stake in Sidanko is up for sale at 110 billion roubles later this month. The winner must also invest at least 325.1 billion roubles in Sidanko.
Russian officials said they were banking on 12.4 trillion roubles in privatisation revenues for 1996.
However, privatisation, which has underpinned Russia's economic reforms, is in limbo. A new minister in charge of sell-offs has yet to be appointed.
